orrowen: Cadhan o hosen re yal cadhat lona
meanings: This we two lay as it was laid for us two: the hearth's closing formula in the dual, as Halyna say it (VI.1, and every Halyna-told leaf)
derivation: a phrase: Cadhan lay-1DU (cadh 'lay' + -An, the 1du ending, broad -an) + o his/it(+S) + hosen as + re PST(+S) + yal S·be.PST + cadhat laid + lona at-1DU (lo + the 1du ending, §3.6); the dual of O0234 Cadhar o hosen re yal cadhat lor, because a Bonded pair speak of themselves as 'we two' (orrowen_v2 §3.9 item 1: where the Book gives Halyna a plural verb, the Orrowen original is dual); unit S10
logogram: TRENN+still (43) + A n · TRENN+still (43) + A t

meanings: We two hold the stone together: Halyna's opening at the hearth (I.4, VI.1)
derivation: a phrase: Kethen hold-1DU (keth 'hold, keep' + -An, slender -en) + et the + tolm stone + olen together (ol 'we' + -en 'of'); unit S10

meanings: The Turn: the subtitle of Book Six (Flennath et Mesk Lurrel)
derivation: a phrase: Et the + Kylyl a turning (kyl 'change; turn' + -Ol, the verbal noun, O1133); unit S10

orrowen: bysket ul lern et trenn hosast
meanings: bound facing the first tale: the Epilogue's heading (Trenn Rask, bysket ul lern et trenn hosast); of a leaf of the Book, bound in facing another
derivation: a phrase: bysket tied, bound (bysk 'tie, knot fast' + -At, O0227) + ul lern in the face of, facing (O2631) + et the + trenn tale + hosast first (hos + -Ast); the leaf of IV.4's headnote 'doss o ul lern Yebb et Pard' faces in the same way; unit S10
logogram: TOVV+cup (170) + A t · VESK+rim (230) · TRENN (39) · FORE (328)

meanings: the Bearer of Branches: the shore's name for Leavaren
derivation: a phrase: Lymmerd bearer (lymm 'bring, bear' + -Ard, O1314) + Yendeth S·gendeth, branches (gend 'a shoot from a stump; a branch, a bough' + -Ath, slender -eth; g > y before a vowel, §3.3), the possessor softened in the construct (§3.2), as Molt Hyll and Meskdhrenn Dholm; unit S10
logogram: PAR+course (98) + A r d · MESK+bough (191) + A th

meanings: the Grain That Rots: the shore's name for Vaelress
derivation: a phrase: Meskdhrenn the grain of wood (O1383) + sa REL(+S) + Lilv rot, go soft (O1205, l unchanged), the relative epithet of §3.10 (X who V), as Harl Orrow sa Vorr and Sulter sa vorr; unit S10

meanings: the Burning: the shore's name for Esthaer
derivation: vorr 'fire; burn' + -Ol, the verbal noun (O2785), used as a name, as the shore's Molt Hyll is a plain construct; unit S10

meanings: the Long Winter: the shore's name for Eirlenth
derivation: a phrase: Grem winter (O0791) + Sell long (O2241), noun and adjective (adjectives do not mutate, §3.3); unit S10

meanings: the Blood of the Sky: the shore's name for Naelthar. The hearth hears it chime with Lodh Helv, the Aetherbond
derivation: a phrase: Lorr blood (O1250) + Helv S·helv, the sky (O0914, h unchanged), the construct (§3.2); unit S10

meanings: the Silvered: the shore's name for Neivaere
derivation: lennet 'silvered' (lenn 'silver' + -At, O1177), used as a name; unit S10

meanings: the Bearer of the Binding: Seren's shore-gloss of the Aelvaren
derivation: a phrase: Lymmerd bearer (lymm + -Ard, O1314) + et the + Lodh the bond (O1221: mortar; a bond; join, bind), the construct with a definite possessor (no mutation after et); unit S10

meanings: those of the breath ('the people of the breath'): Seren's gloss of Naelear
derivation: a phrase: lunt a people (O1283) + et the + hoss breath (O1004), the construct; not *hossan (hoss + -an, 'the breath-folk'), which reads as hoss + -An, 'we two breathe' (lexicon §4.2: a form that collides is not made); unit S10
